title: Conditional variance of a biased Boolean function
statement: Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $p\in(0,1)$, and let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$ be a Boolean function. For every coordinate $i$ and input $x$, the variance of the real-valued function $f$ when coordinate $i$ is resampled from the biased sign law that assigns probability $p$ to $-1$ and $1-p$ to $1$ is $4p(1-p)$ if $f(x)$ changes when coordinate $i$ is flipped, and is $0$ otherwise.
